Union hall. The out-of-work guys/gals sign a list and they are assigned to jobs in that order as contractors request additional manpower.

And to your point about standardized pay scale - I've heard this complaint from a lot of people, most pointedly from the high performers such as yourself, and I don't disagree, but there is some context that is missing, at least in our industry (construction). Yes, the good ones and the not-so-good (or downright lousy) ones may make the same pay per-hour, but they don't work the same amount of hours. There are market pressures pushing in on us from all directions, so the low performers are always the last to get asked to work (including overtime) and the first to get laid off when things wind down, so the effect is that the high performing shitlords and ladies make a lot of money by the end of the year and the low performing tub-o-lards make far less. The foremen talk among themselves, so word gets around about who you want on your crew and who you don't. This point may not hold in factory work - I've never worked in that environment, but the market for construction labor has mostly figured this one out, in a sense.
